title: Older Patients: What Aging Changes, and How the PCP Assesses
next: Chapter 45, Lesson 2: Geriatric emergencies, falls, medications and elder abuse

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already assess older patients with a primary survey, vital signs and a history. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Tell normal aging from illness; see why reserve is low
  2. Recognize atypical presentations: silent MI, pneumonia without fever, delirium
  3. Run a deeper PCP assessment: GEMS, med history, Functional Enquiry

Textbook: Chapter 45, PDF pages 3883–3928
slides.say: Welcome to our chapter on geriatrics, the care of people aged sixty-five and older. As EMRs, you've already cared for many older patients. You know the primary survey, the vital signs, and how to move a frail person gently. Now that you're practising as a PCP, older patients ask more of you. Their illnesses often hide, they take many medications, and you're the one deciding about IV fluids, CPAP and drugs. Today we'll cover three things: how aging changes the body, how illness can look completely different in an older person, and how to do a deeper PCP assessment, including the Functional Enquiry.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到老年医学这一章，也就是对六十五岁及以上人群的照护。作为 EMR，你们已经照顾过很多老年病人：会做初检、测生命体征，也知道怎么轻柔地搬动虚弱的人。现在以 PCP 身份执业，老年病人对你的要求更高：他们的病常常藏起来，吃的药很多，而静脉补液、CPAP 和用药都要由你来决定。今天讲三件事：衰老怎样改变身体；疾病在老人身上怎样可能完全变了样；以及怎样做更深入的 PCP 评估，包括系统问诊（Functional Enquiry）。

slides.title: Aging is not a disease
slides.body:
Getting old does not cause symptoms by itself

  • Normal: slower thinking and recall, less steady balance
  • Not normal: confusion, falls, fainting, incontinence, depression
  • Older adults under-report: they fear losing independence
  • A 9-1-1 call usually means a real problem, maybe not the one they name
slides.say: Here's the key idea of this chapter. Getting old is not a disease, and it doesn't cause symptoms by itself. Normal aging means thinking and remembering a bit more slowly, and balance that's less steady. But confusion, falls, fainting, incontinence and depression are not normal aging. Each one has a cause. Avoid two mistakes: treating normal aging as an illness, and, more dangerous, blaming a real illness on just getting old. Older people also tend to play down their symptoms, often because they fear losing their independence. So when an older adult calls 9-1-1, take it seriously. There's usually a real reason, even if it's not the one they tell you.
slides.sayZh: 先讲本章的核心观念：变老不是病，本身不会产生症状。正常衰老是思考和回忆稍慢一点、平衡没那么稳。但意识混乱、跌倒、晕厥、尿失禁和抑郁都不是正常衰老，每一样都有原因。要避免两种错误：把正常衰老当病来治；以及更危险的——把真正的疾病归咎于「人老了」。老人还常常淡化症状，往往是怕失去独立生活的能力。所以老人打 9-1-1 一定要认真对待：通常确实有事，即使不是他嘴上说的那件事。

slides.title: Less in reserve
slides.body:
Heartless blood per beat, slow rates commonbeta blockers can hide tachycardia
Lungsstiff chest, weak muscles, weak coughPaO₂ ≈ 100 − age ÷ 3 (about 75 at age 80)
Kidneysfewer nephrons, weak thirstdehydrate fast, overload fast

Temperature control weakens too: an infection may bring little or no fever.
slides.say: Why do older patients crash so easily? Because they have less in reserve. The heart pumps less blood with each beat, and slow rates are common, so it can't speed up much to compensate. A beta blocker can hide the fast pulse of shock. The lungs have a stiffer chest and weaker muscles, and the normal oxygen level in arterial blood is lower: roughly one hundred minus a third of the age, so about seventy-five at age eighty. The kidneys lose filtering units and thirst is weak, so dehydration comes fast. But they also can't clear a big salt load, like litres of IV saline, so overload comes fast too. And with weaker temperature control, infections may bring little or no fever.
slides.sayZh: 为什么老年病人这么容易突然垮掉？因为储备少。心脏每搏输出的血更少，心率偏慢也很常见，所以没法靠加快心率来代偿；β 阻滞剂还可能掩盖休克时的快心率。肺部胸廓变硬、呼吸肌变弱，动脉血的正常氧分压也偏低：大约是一百减去年龄的三分之一，八十岁约七十五。肾脏的过滤单位减少，口渴感又弱，所以脱水来得快；但它也排不掉大量的盐，比如几升静脉生理盐水，所以液体超负荷同样来得快。体温调节变弱，感染时可能只有低热甚至不发热。

slides.title: When illness hides
slides.body:
ProblemIn an older adult, may look like
Heart attackno chest pain: short of breath, fainting, weak, confused, nauseated, tired
Pneumonianormal temperature, little cough; confusion, fast breathing
Uncontrolled diabetesHHS rather than DKA: BGL often > 33 mmol/L, dehydration, confusion
Many illnessesdelirium only

Delirium in an older adult = physical illness or drug toxicity. Always an emergency.
slides.say: The second challenge is that disease often looks different in older adults. A heart attack may come with no chest pain at all. Instead, the patient is short of breath, faints, or feels weak, confused, nauseated, or just very tired. Pneumonia may bring a normal temperature and hardly any cough; the only clues may be confusion and fast breathing. Uncontrolled diabetes more often shows up as HHS, hyperglycemic hyperosmolar syndrome, than as DKA, with a sugar often above thirty-three, dehydration and confusion. And many illnesses may show up only as delirium, a sudden, fluctuating confusion. In an older adult, delirium always means physical illness or drug toxicity, and it's always an emergency.
slides.sayZh: 第二个难点是：疾病在老人身上常常换了样子。心梗可能完全没有胸痛，病人只是气短、晕倒，或者觉得无力、糊涂、恶心，或只是特别累。肺炎可能体温正常、几乎不咳，唯一的线索可能就是意识混乱和呼吸快。糖尿病失控更常表现为 HHS，也就是高渗高血糖综合征，而不是 DKA：血糖常高于三十三，伴脱水和意识混乱。很多病都可能只表现为谵妄，也就是突然出现、时好时坏的意识混乱。在老人身上，谵妄一定意味着躯体疾病或药物中毒，而且一定是急症。

slides.q: An 84-year-old woman has been confused and drowsy since yesterday and hasn't eaten. Temp 36.8 °C, RR 28, HR 104, BP 132/74, SpO₂ 92%. No cough, no pain. What's your best interpretation?
options: Her dementia is getting worse, as expected with age
An acute illness such as pneumonia is likely; treat it as an emergency
No fever and no cough rule out an infection
She's just hungry; feed her and leave her at home
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. An eighty-four-year-old woman has been confused and drowsy since yesterday, and she hasn't eaten. Her temperature is thirty-six point eight, breathing rate twenty-eight, heart rate one hundred four, blood pressure one hundred thirty-two over seventy-four, and saturation ninety-two percent. She has no cough and no pain. What's your best interpretation? A, her dementia is getting worse, as expected with age. B, an acute illness such as pneumonia is likely; treat it as an emergency. C, no fever and no cough rule out an infection. D, she's just hungry; feed her and leave her at home. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。一位八十四岁女士从昨天起意识混乱、昏昏欲睡，也没吃东西。体温三十六点八，呼吸二十八，心率一百零四，血压一百三十二比七十四，血氧百分之九十二。没有咳嗽，也没有疼痛。最合理的判断是？A 她的痴呆在加重，人老了就会这样；B 很可能是肺炎之类的急性病，要按急症处理；C 不发热也不咳嗽，就可以排除感染；D 她只是饿了，喂点东西让她留在家。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Confusion that starts over hours to days is delirium, and in an older adult it's an emergency until proven otherwise. Her fast breathing is a sensitive clue to a lung infection, even with a normal temperature and no cough. A is wrong because dementia develops over months to years, not overnight. C is wrong because older adults with pneumonia often have little or no fever. D misses a sick patient; here, not eating is a symptom, not the cause.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。几小时到几天内出现的意识混乱就是谵妄，在老人身上，除非证明不是，否则都按急症对待。呼吸快是肺部感染的敏感线索，即使体温正常、不咳嗽也一样。A 错在痴呆是几个月到几年慢慢形成的，不会一夜之间出现；C 错在老人得肺炎常常只有低热或不发热；D 漏掉了一个病人——这里不吃东西是症状，不是原因。

slides.title: The GEMS diamond
slides.body:
LetterThink about
Geriatricexpect an atypical presentation
Environmentheat or cold, hazards, food in the fridge, bottles
Medicalmany conditions; prescription, OTC and herbal products
Sociallives alone? help with daily activities? referrals

Write what you see at home in the PCR, so social services can follow up.
slides.say: The GEMS diamond is a memory aid for older patients. G is for geriatric: remind yourself that this patient may not present the textbook way. E is for environment. Is the home too hot or too cold? Is it safe, or full of trip hazards? Is there food in the fridge, or a row of empty bottles? M is for medical: several conditions, and many prescription, over-the-counter and herbal products. S is for social: do they live alone, and who helps them dress, shop and eat? You may be the only health worker who ever sees inside the home, so write what you see in your patient care report for social services to follow up.
slides.sayZh: GEMS 菱形是照顾老年病人的记忆口诀。G 代表老年（Geriatric）：提醒自己，这位病人可能不按教科书的样子表现。E 代表环境（Environment）：家里太热还是太冷？安全吗，还是到处是绊倒隐患？冰箱里有吃的吗？还是一排空酒瓶？M 代表医疗（Medical）：多种疾病，还有大量处方药、非处方药和草药。S 代表社会（Social）：是否独居？谁帮他穿衣、买菜、吃饭？你可能是唯一一个进过他家门的医护人员，所以把看到的写进病人护理记录（PCR），方便社会服务跟进。

slides.title: Talking with older patients
slides.body:
• Introduce yourself; use their name, not "dear" or "grandpa"
  • Speak to the patient first: face to face, lights on, slowly
  • Hearing aids and glasses in, and bring them to hospital
  • Assume normal mental status until proven otherwise
  • Check the baseline with family or caregivers
  • Find the new problem: "What's changed since last week?"
slides.say: Introduce yourself and use the patient's name; don't call them dear or grandpa unless they ask you to. Speak to the patient first, not to the family over their head. Sit face to face, turn on the lights, speak slowly and clearly, and then wait for the answer. Put in their hearing aids and glasses, and take them along to the hospital. Here's a key rule: assume the patient's mental status is normal until you have evidence that it isn't, then check with the family what's normal for this person. Many complaints are old ones, so to find the new problem, ask what has changed since last week, and what made them call today.
slides.sayZh: 先自我介绍，称呼病人的名字；除非对方要求，别叫「亲爱的」或「爷爷」。先跟病人本人说话，而不是越过他去跟家属说。面对面坐，开灯，说话慢而清楚，然后等他回答。帮他戴上助听器和眼镜，去医院时一起带上。一条关键原则：先假定病人的精神状态正常，直到有证据表明不是，再向家属确认他平时是什么样。很多主诉是老毛病，要找出新问题，就问和上周比有什么变化、今天是什么让他决定打电话。

slides.title: The medication history matters most
slides.body:
Medications cause a large share of older adults' problems

  • At home: 3–5 drugs a day; nursing home: 6–7 + 2–3 as needed
  • Each drug: name, dose, how often
  • Include OTC (aspirin, antacids), herbal, not-taken and borrowed drugs
  • Look in the bathroom, bedside, kitchen and fridge
  • With permission, bring them all to hospital
slides.say: Of everything in an older adult's history, the medication history matters most, because medications cause a large share of their problems. Older people at home take three to five medications a day on average; nursing home residents take six to seven, plus two or three as needed. Ask about each one by name, dose and how often. Ask about over-the-counter products like aspirin and antacids, herbal remedies, drugs prescribed but not taken, and drugs borrowed from a spouse. Can't find them? Check the bathroom, the bedside table, the kitchen counter and the fridge. As a PCP, this list is your safety check before you give any drug. Next lesson, we'll practise reading it.
slides.sayZh: 老人病史里最重要的是用药史，因为他们的很多问题都是药物引起的。居家老人平均每天吃三到五种药；养老院的老人每天六到七种，外加两三种按需用的。每一种都要问药名、剂量和多久吃一次。还要问非处方药，比如阿司匹林和抗酸药、草药、开了没吃的药，以及从配偶那里借来吃的药。找不到药？去看浴室药柜、床头柜、厨房台面和冰箱。作为 PCP，这张药单是你给任何药之前的安全检查。下节课我们来练习怎么读它。

slides.title: Vital signs that can fool you
slides.body:
• Baseline BP runs high: systolic < 120 may mean hypovolemia
  • Ask their usual BP; consider both arms
  • Big drop on sitting up: low volume or too much medication
  • Fast breathing may be the only sign of pneumonia
  • Crackles may be normal for age; ankle swelling may be old vein disease

BC exam: auscultate at least 6 points, front or back.
slides.say: In older adults, blood pressure usually runs high, so a number that looks normal can be low for this patient. The book's rule: think of hypovolemia in any older person with a systolic under one hundred twenty, and try to find out their usual pressure. A big drop when they sit up points to low volume or too much medication. Watch the breathing rate; fast breathing may be the only sign of pneumonia. Some findings look worse than they are: crackles at the lung bases can be normal for age, and swollen ankles may come from old vein problems, not heart failure. For the BC exam, listen at least six points on the front or six on the back.
slides.sayZh: 老人的血压通常偏高，所以看起来正常的数字，对这位病人可能已经偏低。书里的原则：任何收缩压低于一百二十的老人都要想到低血容量，并尽量问清他平时的血压。坐起来时血压明显下降，提示容量不足或用药过量。注意呼吸频率：呼吸快可能是肺炎唯一的征象。也有些发现看着吓人其实未必：肺底的湿啰音可能是老年人的正常现象，脚踝肿可能是陈旧的静脉问题，而不是心衰。BC 考试要记住：肺部听诊至少前胸六个点或后背六个点。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: assessing an older patient
slides.body:
BC assessment model: the secondary survey is history, vital signs, head-to-toe exam and, for PCPs, the Functional Enquiry.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Primary survey; fix problems as found
  • History; pain by OPQRRRST or LOTARP
  • Vital signs, SpO₂; glucose when LOC is down
  • Head-to-toe exam; reassess; transport

PCP adds

  • Functional Enquiry: 9 systems (PCP only)
  • Med list checked against PCP drug contraindications
  • IV and fluids when a protocol calls for them
  • CPAP only when BC criteria are met
slides.say: Here's how your assessment changes as a PCP. The left column is what every licence level does: the primary survey, a history, with OPQRRRST or LOTARP for any pain, vital signs with oxygen saturation, a glucose check when the level of consciousness is down, a head-to-toe exam, reassessment and transport. The right column is new for you. In BC's assessment model, the Functional Enquiry is required for PCPs only. You check the medication list against the contraindications of every drug you're about to give. You start an IV and give fluids when a protocol calls for them. And you decide on CPAP, but only when the BC criteria are met. With older patients, each of these needs extra care.
slides.sayZh: 看看作为 PCP，你的评估怎么变。左栏是所有执照级别都做的：初检；问病史，疼痛用 OPQRRRST 或 LOTARP；测生命体征和血氧；意识下降时测血糖；从头到脚体检；复评和转运。右栏是你新增的：在 BC 评估模型里，系统问诊只要求 PCP 做。你要把药单和准备给的每一种药的禁忌症逐一对照；按流程需要时开静脉、补液；还要判断是否上 CPAP，但只有符合 BC 标准时才上。对老年病人，每一项都要格外小心。

slides.title: The Functional Enquiry, older-adult style
slides.body:
SystemAsk, for example
General healthappetite, weight, energy, recent falls
CNSdizzy spells, fainting, new confusion, weakness, speech
Respiratoryshort of breath when? cough, sputum colour, sleeps sitting up?
Cardiovascularchest, arm or jaw pain; fluttering; ankle swelling
GI / GUnausea, bowel changes, black stool; trouble urinating
Skin, MSKskin tears, bruises, sores; new pain, can't bear weight
Endocrine, EENTdiabetes, thirst; vision, hearing, swallowing

BC grading: system not asked −5%, related detail missed −3%, unrelated −1%; max −15%. No deduction if no history can be obtained.
slides.say: BC's grading sheet lists nine systems for the PCP's Functional Enquiry: general health, the central nervous system, respiratory, cardiovascular, GI and GU, skin, musculoskeletal, endocrine, and eyes, ears, nose and throat. With older patients it's especially valuable, because the chief complaint often sounds minor while the real problem hides in another system. Ask about appetite, weight and recent falls; dizzy spells and new confusion; when they get short of breath, and whether they now sleep sitting up, which suggests heart failure; black stools; trouble passing urine; skin tears and bruises. On the exam, a system you don't ask about costs five percent, up to fifteen percent in total. If no history can be obtained, there's no deduction.
slides.sayZh: BC 评分表列出 PCP 系统问诊的九个系统：全身情况、中枢神经、呼吸、心血管、消化和泌尿生殖、皮肤、肌肉骨骼、内分泌，以及眼耳鼻喉。对老年病人它特别有用，因为主诉听起来常常是小事，真正的问题却藏在别的系统里。问问食欲、体重和最近有没有跌倒；有没有头晕发作、新出现的糊涂；什么时候会气短，现在是不是要坐着睡——那提示心衰；有没有黑便；排尿困难；皮肤撕裂和瘀青。考试时，漏问一个系统扣百分之五，整个系统问诊最多扣百分之十五；完全无法获得病史时不扣分。

slides.q: You're the PCP for an 88-year-old woman who fell but wasn't hurt. RR 16, SpO₂ 96% on room air, no distress. You hear fine crackles at both lung bases. What's your best decision?
options: Start CPAP at 5 cmH₂O right away
Note the crackles, look for other signs and reassess; CPAP isn't indicated
Give a 500 mL fluid bolus to support her blood pressure
The crackles prove heart failure; transport with lights and sirens
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. You're caring for an eighty-eight-year-old woman who fell but wasn't hurt. Her breathing rate is sixteen, her saturation is ninety-six percent on room air, and she's in no distress. You hear fine crackles at both lung bases. What's your best decision? A, start CPAP at five centimetres of water right away. B, note the crackles, look for other signs and reassess; CPAP isn't indicated. C, give a five-hundred-millilitre fluid bolus to support her blood pressure. D, the crackles prove heart failure, so transport with lights and sirens. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。你在照顾一位八十八岁、跌倒但没受伤的女士。她呼吸十六次，呼吸室内空气时血氧百分之九十六，没有窘迫。你听到双肺底有细湿啰音。最好的决定是？A 马上上 CPAP，压力五厘米水柱；B 记录啰音，寻找其他征象并复评，现在不符合 CPAP 指征；C 给五百毫升补液支持血压；D 有啰音就证明是心衰，开灯鸣笛转运。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Crackles can be normal in older adults, and the book warns against starting CPAP at the first crackle you hear. BC's CPAP criteria need all of these: a breathing rate over twenty-four, a saturation under ninety-four percent on oxygen, and accessory muscle use. She has none of them, so A is wrong. C is wrong because there's no sign of low volume, and extra saline could tip an older patient into fluid overload. D jumps to a diagnosis from one finding instead of the whole picture.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。湿啰音在老人可以是正常的，书里也提醒别一听到啰音就上 CPAP。BC 的 CPAP 标准要求同时满足：呼吸超过二十四、吸氧下血氧低于百分之九十四、辅助呼吸肌参与。她一条都不符合，所以 A 错。C 错在没有任何容量不足的征象，多余的生理盐水反而可能让老人液体超负荷。D 凭一个发现就下诊断，没有看整体。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Saline in steps: reassess every 500 mL, listen for new crackles
  • Shock may start above 90 systolic: BC lets you start the protocol early
  • CPAP needs RR > 24, SpO₂ < 94% on O₂ and accessory muscles
  • Beta blockers can hide the fast pulse of shock
  • New confusion: check glucose, SpO₂, temperature, med list
slides.say: Now the new risks that come with your PCP tools. First, saline. Older kidneys can't clear a big salt load, so give fluid in steps, reassess every five hundred millilitres as BC requires, and listen to the lungs each time for new crackles. Second, low pressure is relative. BC's hypovolemia protocol usually starts at a systolic under ninety, but you may start it earlier when you expect shock from the mechanism, the injuries or the patient's condition. Third, CPAP needs all of its criteria; crackles alone are not enough. Fourth, a beta blocker can hide the fast pulse of shock. And fifth, new confusion means checking glucose, oxygen, temperature and the medication list.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲随 PCP 新工具而来的新风险。第一，生理盐水：老人的肾脏排不掉大量的盐，所以补液要分步给，按 BC 要求每五百毫升复评一次，每次都听肺，看有没有新出现的湿啰音。第二，低血压是相对的：BC 低血容量流程一般从收缩压低于九十开始，但如果根据受伤机制、伤情或病人状况预计会休克，可以提前启动。第三，CPAP 要满足全部标准，光有啰音不够。第四，β 阻滞剂可能掩盖休克时的快心率。第五，新出现的意识混乱，要查血糖、血氧、体温和药单。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Aging isn't a disease: confusion, falls and fainting always have a cause
  2. Illness hides: silent MI, pneumonia without fever, delirium; systolic < 120 may be shock
  3. PCP adds the Functional Enquiry and a med check; fluids in small steps

Next: geriatric emergencies, falls, medications and elder abuse
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: aging is not a disease. Confusion, falls and fainting always have a cause, so look for it. Two: illness hides in older adults. Think of a heart attack without chest pain, pneumonia without fever, and delirium as the only sign. A systolic under one hundred twenty may already be shock. Three: as a PCP, you add the Functional Enquiry and a careful medication check, and you give fluids in small steps with frequent reassessment. Next lesson, we'll look at common geriatric emergencies, falls and head injuries, how to read a medication list against your PCP drugs, and elder abuse. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三件事。一，衰老不是病：意识混乱、跌倒、晕厥一定有原因，要去找。二，疾病在老人身上会藏起来：想想没有胸痛的心梗、不发热的肺炎，以及只表现为谵妄的各种病；收缩压低于一百二十可能已经是休克。三，作为 PCP，你多了系统问诊和仔细的药物核对，补液要小量分步、勤复评。下节课讲常见的老年急症、跌倒和头部外伤、怎样拿药单对照你的 PCP 药物，以及老人虐待。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
